subject: literature
passage: The storm had brought down the old treehouse, and in the morning Dev and his brother Rohan stood under the oak looking at the pile of splintered boards. Rohan wanted to haul the wreck to the curb and forget about it. Dev had other ideas. He sorted out the boards that could be reused, sketched a new platform on an envelope, and began pulling bent nails out of the wood. Where Rohan saw only a loss, Dev saw ______.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The last sentence contrasts the brothers. Rohan wants to throw the wreck away, while Dev sorts usable boards and sketches a new platform. Dev sees a chance to build something new, so the blank needs "an opportunity."
explanation.A: Incorrect. There is nothing puzzling about the wreck; the text says the storm brought it down.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Dev is not treating the fallen treehouse as a danger to avoid; he is planning to build again.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Seeing the wreck as a burden is close to Rohan's view, who wants to be rid of it, not the contrasting view Dev holds.
explanation.D: Correct. Dev starts planning and salvaging materials for a new treehouse, so he sees the wreck as an opportunity.
